title: Read Along, Learn Vocabulary, and Practice Grammar Easily!

lines.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to a new episode
of Bo's Slow English. Today, I'm going
to read a story to you and you will have
the opportunity to follow along and read
with me. First, I will read the story at
a normal pace. Then, I will read it
again at a slower pace and break the
story down for you so that you can fully
comprehend it. Lastly, I will read it
again at a normal pace, but this time
you should be able to understand the
story better since we had broken it
down. Are you ready? Here we go. Emma
lives in a small town by the sea. She
loves to watch the waves crash against
the rocks. Every morning, she wakes up
early to see the sunrise. The air is
cool and the world feels quiet. The
early bird catches the worm. Her
grandmother always says, so Emma starts
her day with a smile.
One morning, Emma decides to go fishing.
She grabs her fishing rod and walks down
the beach. The sky is blue and the sun
is bright. She finds a spot near the
pier and sets up her fishing line. It's
peaceful and she enjoys the gentle
sounds of the water.
As Emma waits, she notices a family of
ducks swimming nearby. She hears a loud
splash. One duck dives into the water
and comes up with a fish in its mouth.
Well, that's one way to catch breakfast,
Emma thinks with a laugh.
A few minutes later, she feels a little
pull on her line. Her heart starts to
race. Is it a big fish? She pulls her
fishing rod and slowly reels it in. She
catches a small fish and she's proud of
her work. Emma decides to let the fish
go back
She watches as it swims away. She didn't
keep her catch, but she feels happy.
Sometimes, it's not about what you get,
but what you give, she whispers to
herself.
Emma walks home as the sun gets higher
in the sky.
She thinks about how beautiful the day
is.
Home is where the heart is, she thinks.
Today was a good day. She can't wait to
come back tomorrow.
Okay, I know that was pretty fast. So,
now we're going to read it together
slowly
and then I will break down some of the
idioms as well as some of the more
trickier words. Ready to read along?

Did you notice how my intonation, which
is the up and down sound of my voice,
changed throughout the sentences? A long
time ago, I used to work with Koreans
and when I taught them English, they
noticed that English pronunciation
sounds quite monotone. What that means
is it has a flat type of tone, one tone.
So, in order to sound a little bit more
interesting when speaking English,
sometimes we will put some changes in
the intonation so that we sound less
monotone. Let's go over a few vocabulary
words. Waves, the moving water in the
sea or ocean. Sunrise, when the sun
first appears in the morning. Pier, a
long platform that goes out into the
water, often used for fishing or docking
boats. Fishing rod, a tool used to catch
fish. Reels in, to pull in the fishing
line to bring in the fish. Did you
notice there were a few common idioms
thrown into the story. An idiom is a
phrase or expression that has a
figurative meaning that is different
from the literal meaning of the words in
the phrase. The two idioms in this story
were the early bird catches the worm.
This means that people who get up early
or start something first usually get the
best results. Home is where the heart
is. This means that home is the place
where you feel comfortable and happy.
Did you notice that there were a few
homophones in the story? Homophones are
two words that sound the same, but have
different meanings. So, it is important
when you're writing English that you
choose the correct homophone. For
example, sea and see. Sea refers to the
ocean and see means to look at
something. Sun and son. Sun is the
bright star in the sky during the day
and son is a boy child. In addition,
there were a few contractions.
Contractions are two words that are
smashed together making one word. The
contractions in this story were it's,
which is it is, it's peaceful by the
beach. Didn't,
did not, she didn't keep her catch.
